articles.title: Gravity, damping and friction
articles.summary: The SDK documents world gravity, vehicle damping and surface friction. The game runs a Bullet world with gravity (0, -10, 0) m/s², fixed solver substeps, damping (1 - d)^dt and contact friction clamp(μA × μB, -10, 10).
articles.body: The SDK gives gravity as 10.0, linear and angular damping as 0.1, and surface friction as 0.8. Its linear damping comment says the value tends toward zero with atmospheric height. These are SDK defaults and configuration entries, not measurements of the running simulation. A native decode (investigation/wheels.md, shown on the Wheels parts pages) found that the game builds a Bullet btSoftRigidDynamicsWorld with a btSequentialImpulseConstraintSolver and sets world gravity to (0, -10, 0) m/s², with Y up. The game_constants binder reads gravity, vehicle_linear_damping, vehicle_angular_damping and vehicle_friction by name, with built-in defaults 10, 0.1, 0.1 and 0.8, and each vehicle passes its configured gravity to its bodies. Projectiles do not use the world gravity: their own integration applies 30 m/s² (investigation/weapons.md). Time steps are fixed (investigation/update-rate.md). Components update 60 times per simulated second; the solver accumulates elapsed time and runs whole substeps of 1/60, 1/120 or 1/180 s, from the 60, 120 or 180 Hz setting, at most 1000 per tick, keeping the remainder for the next tick. Each solver step multiplies a body's linear and angular velocity by (1 - d)^dt, with d clamped to 0 to 1, so the default 0.1 keeps 0.9 of the speed per simulated second at every solver rate. The vehicle body build multiplies the linear damping by (1 - 0.0000224138 × y)^5.3595 below a transformed height y of 40000 and uses 0 above it, which matches the SDK comment (inference: y is the height in metres). Contact friction combines the two bodies' coefficients as clamp(μA × μB, -10, 10) and restitution as their product, so vehicle on vehicle at the default 0.8 gives 0.64. Bullet's own construction default is 0.5. Wheels add a sphere body with friction 0.001 but take their grip from a separate ray request (see Wheels, grip and suspension).

Still not recovered: the solver's normal and tangent impulse iterations, its friction-row bounds, collision-shape coverage and restitution threshold, and the rule by which mass redistribution rewrites a vehicle's gravity.

articles.title: Air drag and lift tuning
articles.summary: Hull air drag and lift read built-in game_constants defaults, including air density 1.225. The executable never reads calculate_air_density, so the realtime 0 switches nothing off.
articles.body: The SDK describes linear and quadratic speed factors for pressure and suction drag. The SDK labels 15 m/s as the aerodynamic-force threshold and 50 m/s as the high-speed scaling threshold. A scale of 8 is described as additive. A native decode (investigation/config.md) found where the hull air path reads these values. The vehicle buoyancy and drag routine 0x14048ad30 reads the pressure and suction drag factors 0.05, 0.1, 0.025 and 0.05, the falloff powers 0.6 and 0.4, air_drag_factor 0.2, the three speed settings and air_density from the native constants block. The hull air callback 0x14048e2d0 reads viscous_air_resistance 0.25 and lift_force 0.25. The game sets these constants itself and overrides them only from rom/data/game_constants.xml, which this installation does not ship, so the built-in values apply: air density 1.225, and the same drag and threshold numbers as the SDK. The name calculate_air_density does not occur in the executable as ASCII or UTF-16LE text. The realtime file that sets it to 0 is parsed into a registry that no recovered gameplay code reads. So the 0 does not set a vacuum, switch off air density or disable altitude effects. The realtime file also lists matching drag and threshold values; the hull path reads the native block, not those entries. A separate native decode of the wing, control-surface and fin air routine (investigation/control-surfaces.md, shown on the Control surfaces parts page) found that it multiplies by its own constant 24 and never reads lift_force, so the SDK description of lift_force as surface lift scaling does not hold for those parts. That routine applies an altitude pressure ratio without checking calculate_air_density. The only recovered lift_force read is in the hull air callback.

articles.title: Buoyancy and water drag
articles.summary: Buoyancy pushes up with water_density × g × V ÷ D, where D rises from 10 to 20 as body mass goes from 2000 to 25000. The unmodified game uses the built-in multiplier 10; the realtime file's 12 has no recovered reader.
articles.body: The SDK documents water density as 1000 and exposes separate pressure, suction, viscous and wave-slamming terms. A native decode (investigation/config.md) recovered the buoyancy routine 0x14048ad30 and its water surface callback 0x14048d4d0. Buoyancy: each body gets an upward force water_density × g × V ÷ D. m is the body mass, g its gravity scalar and V a submerged weight summed over an eight-child spatial tree of the body; a partly submerged leaf counts clamp((h - y + r) ÷ 2r, 0, 1) of its weight, h being the sampled water height, y the node centre and r its half-size. D = buoyancy_mass_multiplier + buoyancy_mass_modifier × clamp((m - buoyancy_mass_modifier_lower) ÷ buoyancy_mass_modifier_upper, 0, 1)^buoyancy_mass_modifier_pow. With the defaults 10, 10, 2000, 23000 and 1 this is D = 10 + 10 × clamp((m - 2000) ÷ 23000, 0, 1): D is 10 up to mass 2000 and reaches 20 at 25000, not at 23000. For V = 1 and g = 10 the upward force is 1000 at mass 100, 666.6667 at 13500 and 500 from 25000 on, in internal units. A larger buoyancy_mass_multiplier lowers the force. The force acts at the submerged centroid, so it also makes a torque, and the game adds it to the Bullet force accumulator; it does not set a velocity. Which multiplier applies: the game sets 10 itself and overrides it only from rom/data/game_constants.xml, which this installation does not ship. The SDK copy, also 10, is not on that path. The realtime file's 12 sits in a registry that the release parses but no recovered gameplay code reads, so this build does not use 12. Compartments: a separate loop adds a downward term -g × water_density × 0.01 × (water_compartment_force_factor × W + gas_compartment_force_factor × G) ÷ D. Both factors default to 1 and are missing from the SDK file. W and G are values returned by two fluid compartment getters; G has a stored field ÷ 60 subtracted and is floored at 0. Water drag: the surface callback subtracts 0.5 × the sampled wave velocity from the point velocity, and the vertical part of that term is scaled by 0.3 when it points down (inference: the sampled vector is the wave velocity). With s the relative speed and d the cosine between the flow and the surface normal, a face with d > 0 gets a pressure force A × d^2.5 × (15 s + 17 s²) against its normal and any other face a suction force A × (-d)^0.3 × (12 s + 5 s²) along it, A being the surface weight. Water density does not multiply these two terms. A viscous term opposes motion with viscous_resistance_factor 0.5 × K × 0.00075 × (20 ÷ (s L × 1000000 + 10) + 1.5) × A × water_density × s², L being a body length scalar. K rises from water_drag_factor 1 at mass 2000 to 5 at 25000 (multiplier 4); those two mass thresholds are built into the code and do not follow the buoyancy settings. Partly submerged faces add a slamming term scaled by slamming_force_multiplier 100 and body mass. The sum of the three terms is capped at s × m × 0.5 ÷ 60. The realtime switches apply_drag, apply_viscous_resistance, apply_slamming_force and use_accurate_buoyancy do not occur in the executable; the callback gates its terms by speed and geometry instead.

articles.title: Wheels, grip and suspension
articles.summary: Realtime configuration separates tire damping, suspension stiffness and wheel torque scaling, but the executable contains none of these names; the wheel code uses its own constants.
articles.body: The shipped tuning includes suspension stiffness 0.2 and damping 1, tire stiffness 1 and damping 4, tire_max_friction 100, tire_grip_multiplier 50 and wheel drive torque multiplier 0.0004. None of these seven names occurs in the executable, in ASCII or UTF-16LE, so nothing shows that this build reads them. A native decode of the advanced wheel update (investigation/wheels.md, shown on the Wheels parts pages) found its own constants instead. Units: the working radius r = wheel_radius - 0.125 + 0.125 × wheel_size is in metres, and the tyre surface moves at 2π × r × RPS m/s, 2.199 to 6.597 m/s per RPS for the road wheels at the default wheel_size 1. Speed dependence: the slip velocity between ground and tyre is capped at 5 m/s, so the grip request grows with slip up to 5 m/s and stays flat beyond it. The request is Q = (50 × grip_factor × tyre factor ÷ r) × (2000 q + 100 u), with u the slip and q the contact drift since the last update, at most 0.1 × r and scaled by the brake. The tyre factor is 1, or 1.75 for a double wheel, times 0.25, 0.1875 or 0.125 by tyre type; tank wheels halve it outside a track. Contact: each wheel casts a ray to the ground and also carries a sphere body with Bullet friction 0.001. The contact feeds the shaft: the wheel adds slip ÷ (2π × r) × tyre factor × grip_factor × 0.5 to its RPS and submits that RPS with a weight equal to its definition mass, × 0.7 with suspension. Suspension: the ray spring pushes with 60 × tyre_pressure × (k × max(0, 1.5 × r - l) + c × (l_old - l)), l being the ray distance, k = 0.05 + 0.45 × stiffness_factor and c = 0.5 + 4.5 × damping_factor; wheels without suspension set k and c to 0. Maximum friction: the file's 100 is not a Coulomb limit the code reads. The wheel code's own 100 is the slip gain and the 100 × r slip cap, and the request has no normal-load input. The file's 50 and 4 equal the code's grip scale and tyre damping factor, but the code holds them as built-in numbers.

articles.title: Diesel engine connections and startup
articles.summary: Engine definitions describe separate air, fuel, exhaust, coolant and electrical connections.
articles.body: The small engine accepts throttle from 0 to 1. Its starter description says electrical power increases engine RPS for startup. Coolant has separate cold return and hot output ports. The small and large definitions set engine_max_force to 20000 and 200000 respectively. A separate native decode of the classic engine update (investigation/classic-engines.md, shown on the Diesel Engine parts page) found that this field sets the shaft weight, scales diesel and intake demand and multiplies the starter charge request. It is an internal solver weight, not a torque in N m. A later decode (investigation/drivetrain-gaps.md) found that the limiter and the combustion gate compare signed speed, so a shaft turning backward gets no throttle cut and no combustion gain: the engine's own speed candidate is 0.99 × r and decays toward 0 unless the shaft keeps driving it. Heating uses |r| and still applies. The speed branch does not replace NaN or infinity, and a connected shaft replaces the local speed with its group's published speed.

articles.title: Modular engine assembly and telemetry
articles.summary: Cylinder tooltips describe manifold sharing, and composite output names three data channels.
articles.body: The 1x1 cylinder attaches to a crankshaft and needs manifolds for air, fuel and exhaust. Directly adjacent cylinders can share a manifold according to the supplied tooltip. Cylinder composite values 1, 2 and 3 are air volume, fuel volume and temperature. The starter attaches to a drive belt, and the alternator converts drive belt energy to electric charge. A native decode (investigation/modular-engines.md, shown on the Modular engines parts pages) found how these parts assemble and what the channels hold. Parts joined by crankshaft, belt and cylinder couplings share one crank RPS with inertia I = 1 + the sum of their engine_max_force; parts joined by manifold couplings share one temperature, heat capacity and throttle pair. Each cylinder needs the crank above 2 RPS and its air:fuel ratio inside 12 - 2t to 16 + 4t, with t = manifold °C ÷ 100 clamped to 0 to 1. Its efficiency is a speed factor times 1 - 2 (s - 0.6)², so the best ratio is 13.6 + 0.4t, 13.68 at 20 °C and 14 from 100 °C; the inspected Stoichiometric value 2s - 1 then reads 0.2. An undamaged cylinder adds 80000 × burned fuel × efficiency ÷ I RPS per update, where burned fuel is RPS × 0.000004 × voxels × fuel throttle while the crank is at most 60 RPS and the exhaust has room. Composite value 1 is 6000 × the admitted oxygen, value 2 is 10 × the admitted diesel in litres and value 3 is the manifold temperature in °C. Values 1 and 2 are per cylinder visit, not per second, and value 1 ÷ value 2 is the air:fuel ratio.

articles.title: Speed, altitude and radar signals
articles.summary: Selected sensor descriptions state their units and radar input ranges.
articles.body: Linear speed uses m/s. Angular speed uses rotations per second, and its tooltip names the component y axis. Altitude is metres above sea level. The selected short range radar uses turns for yaw and elevation, with FOV input 0.01 to 0.125 and facing yaw -0.5 to 0.5. Its radar_range field is 5000. That value alone does not guarantee a detection distance for any target. A native decode of the advanced radars (definition type 56: Basic, AWACS, Dish, Phalanx and Missile; investigation/sensors-radio.md, shown on the Other components parts page) found that they also report angles in turns, dividing by 2π. Their working range is R = radar_range × 0.02 × 0.02 ÷ (FOV x × FOV y) on the native FOV fields, a new scan runs every max(1, floor(R ÷ 2000 + 0.5)) updates, and a target passes when its distance is at most R and R ÷ 10000 × signature ÷ distance exceeds 0.025. At the SDK defaults reported distances carry up to ±1% noise and angles up to ±0.001 turn. A later decode (investigation/sensors-legacy.md, shown on the Other components and legacy radar parts pages) found that the signature is the target's physics-body mass, built from the components' definition mass, and that the editor's FOV sliders set each advanced axis from 0.01 to 0.25. It also covers the short range radar here, a legacy type-16 radar: a target passes when signature ÷ distance exceeds 0.25, inside a far plane radar_range × (0.75 + 0.25 × 0.01 ÷ saved radar_fov) ahead, about 3875 m at the saved default 0.1, and inside side planes set by the FOV input. No scan counter precedes its candidate collection, so (inference) it collects on every update that passes its power and height gates. A later static decode (investigation/force-cap.md, shown on the Altimeter and Linear Speed Sensor parts pages) found that the altimeter outputs the part's world Y: height above the fixed sea-level datum y = 0, not clearance over terrain or the local wave surface. It outputs 0 above a height of 40000 or at world X above 156000. The linear speed sensor outputs the physics velocity of its own point, body velocity plus angular velocity × lever arm, in m/s. It does not difference positions, smooth or subtract wind; its four modes give the full speed, the component along its axis, the horizontal speed and the vertical speed. Both are recomputed on every logic update, 60 per simulated second, with no sensor timer of their own. The advanced radar's line-of-sight query filters by collision bits: an object can block only when its collision group lacks bit 0x1000 and shares a bit with 0xff, and its object mask shares a bit with 0x7f. Render materials and transparency take no part in that test.

articles.title: Radar and sonar output noise
articles.summary: The SDK noise settings bound a uniform random error on advanced radar distance and on advanced radar and sonar angles; legacy radars and sonars add none.
articles.body:
The SDK documents sonar_noise and radar_noise as positive and negative ranges of small discrepancies in reported positions. Both defaults are 0.001. It separately describes radar_distance_noise, default 0.01, as a maximum percentage discrepancy in reported distance. A native decode of the advanced radar and sonar (investigation/sensors-radio.md, shown on the Other components parts page) found that the game reads all three names from data/game_constants.xml, with built-in fallbacks 0.001, 0.001 and 0.01, and applies them to each output value with a fresh random U from 0 to 1. Radar distance becomes distance × (1 - D + 2D U) with D = radar_distance_noise, so ±1% at the default. Each radar and sonar angle, in turns, gets -A + 2A U with A = radar_noise or sonar_noise, so ±0.001 turn (±0.36 degrees). Sonar outputs get no distance noise. U = (random integer & 32767) ÷ 32767, so the error stays inside that band.

A later decode (investigation/leftovers.md) recovered the random routine: state = 214013 × state + 2531011 modulo 2^32, returning (state >> 16) & 32767. The noise variable 2U - 1 therefore takes 32768 equally spaced values from -1 to 1. The generator runs through all 2^32 states before repeating, so over one cycle each value occurs equally often. The error is uniform across the band, not Gaussian, and the draws are a fixed sequence from the seed, not independent samples. The same decode found that the legacy radars and sonars (definition type 16, logic case 50) add no SDK noise: they write the geometric distance and angles straight to their outputs and never read these settings.

articles.title: PID controller state and signals
articles.summary: The controller definition says disabling Active resets stored values.
articles.body: The PID takes a measured Process Variable and desired Setpoint, then exposes Control Output. Its Active description explicitly says stored values reset when inactive. The tooltip allows setting proportional, integral and derivative terms with the select tool. The Boolean capacitor is a separate logic component whose signal charges and discharges stored state. A separate native decode of the logic update (investigation/logic.md, shown on the PID Controller parts page) found a per-update recurrence: e = Setpoint - Process Variable, S = S + e, and Control Output = Ki × S + Kp × e + Kd × (e - e_prev) in single precision. There is no time step: at 60 updates per simulated second S gains 60 errors per second, and the derivative is the change over one update. The derivative is 0 on the first active update and has no filter. Turning Active off sets S, the previous error and the output to 0. The physical PID clamps S to ± max_error ÷ max(1e-8, Ki) when max_error is above 0 and turns a NaN or infinite output into 0; it does not limit the output itself. The microprocessor PIDs skip both steps. The capacitor counts whole updates, trunc(60 × charge or discharge time), and its stored charge is a Boolean, so it says nothing about electrical batteries.

articles.title: Base fuel inventory transfers
articles.summary: The storage addon transfers fuel between named vehicle tanks and tile inventories, each port once every 60 onTick callbacks.
articles.body: Storage staggers ports by vehicle ID modulo 60 against a callback counter, so a port is handled on one onTick callback in 60. The counter ignores game_ticks, so the period is 60 callbacks; how long that takes depends on how often the engine calls onTick. Diesel input adds the tank's whole diesel entry to the tile inventory, with no per-callback limit, then requests 0 fresh water and 0 nitrogen in the inlet. Jet input does the same with the jet fuel entry. Diesel output computes the free space as capacity minus the tank's total value, clamps it to the tile's diesel stock, subtracts that delta from the stock and requests old total plus delta of the tank's current dominant fluid_type, then 0 nitrogen. Jet output does the same with jet fuel. Inputs run before outputs, so fuel credited by an inlet can leave through an outlet in the same callback. Example: an outlet of capacity 100 holding 40 with 25 in stock requests 65 and leaves 0 in stock. The output request uses the tank's reported fluid_type, so a diesel outlet holding mostly jet fuel debits diesel stock while asking for more jet fuel. A native decode (investigation/small-parts.md) found that server.setVehicleTank does not write the tank itself. Its binding resolves the named tank and appends a 36-byte request, kind 2, holding the vehicle ID, voxel position, value and fluid ID, to a queue; the tank changes only when that queue is applied. A later decode (investigation/fluid-gaps.md) followed the queue to the tank. A setter request has no delay, and ready requests are applied in queue order, so two requests to one tank are neither reordered nor merged. The application scales the value by 0.1 to a stored amount and clamps it to 0 … tank volume. It sets every species of the requested one's class, liquid or gas, to 0, adds the clamped amount to the requested species and recomputes the total. The other class and the temperature stay as they were. Only fixed fluid and gas tanks are written, and fluid IDs of 13 or more are rejected. For this script that means the inlet's 0 fresh-water request clears every liquid in the inlet while only the diesel or jet fuel entry was credited, so water or another fuel in an inlet is lost, and the 0 nitrogen request clears every gas. An outlet's fill replaces its whole liquid class with old total plus delta of its fluid_type, and the following 0 nitrogen request clears gases without touching that liquid. Nothing is rolled back: the script changes its tile inventory when it queues the requests, and a request that later fails, because the vehicle is not loaded or the target is not a fixed tank or the fluid ID is out of range, is dropped without undoing that change. This is addon bookkeeping rather than the fluid network solver.

articles.title: Weather temperature, lighting and hazards
articles.summary: Parts sample a weather temperature that blends air and water by depth: air follows a warmth fraction from world Z, scrolling weather textures, month and time of day, minus rain cooling and 6.5 °C per 1000 m of height. The native lighting table and the tornado, whirlpool and tsunami vectors are decoded; the realtime environment file's hour markers and force terms are not what the game uses. While a tornado exists, vehicles also get a direct wind force that skips the joined-mass force cap. Two shipped addons spawn natural disasters and native code spreads forest fires; each hazard has a decoded reach or an open item.
articles.body:
Every part that samples its surroundings outside an enclosed compartment (heat exchangers, radiators, engines, fluid tanks, steam and nuclear parts) uses one weather routine. It blends an air temperature Ta and a water temperature Tw by f = clamp((h − y + 0.25) ÷ 24, 0, 1), with h the wave-surface height and y the sample height, so the sample is pure air from 0.25 m above the surface and pure water from 23.75 m below it.

Both temperatures start from a regional sampler that returns a warmth fraction W and a rain value R, each 0 to 1. W = clamp(1 − 6 × |z ÷ 256000 + 0.5 − 0.35| + a + 0.475 × season + 0.05 × day, 0, 1). The first term is a band along world Z, highest at z = −38400 m (inference: a latitude-like climate band). a is the product of two red samples of the noise texture weather_1.txtr, read at a fast and a slow scrolling offset; R comes from its green samples as clamp(5 × (g1 − 0.15), 0, 1). World X enters only through the textures. day = 0.5 + 0.5 × sin(2π × q − π/2) is 0 at midnight and 1 at noon, with q the fraction of the game day. season = 0.5 + 0.5 × sin(0.5711987 × (month + q) − π/2) peaks at month + q = 5.5. It reads the saved month and the fraction of the day but not the day of the month, so it advances over each day and steps back at midnight unless the month changes (inference from the formula).

Air: Ta = max(−270, lerp(−15 − 15k, 30 − 10k, W) − 6.5 × max(y, 0) ÷ 1000), with k = (0.8 × clamp((R − 0.4) ÷ 0.6, 0, 1) + 0.2 × w)³. Parts pass a flag that fixes w at 0.1, so wind never changes a part's sample (12 of the 13 calls found pass it). Dry air therefore runs from −15 °C at W = 0 to 30 °C at W = 1 at sea level, and heavy rain (R = 1) moves those ends to −23.27 and 24.49 °C. Height above world zero costs 6.5 °C per 1000 m. Water: Tw = lerp(1 − 4R, 8 − 5R, W) + 3 × (D ÷ 1000) × (0.5 − W), with D = max(−y, 0) metres below world zero, not below the local wave surface. There is no depth clamp and no lower floor; depth warms water where W < 0.5 and cools it where W > 0.5, by at most 1.5 °C per 1000 m.

Without rain a part reads −15 + 45 × W to within 0.001 °C. At a location where W = 0.5 at midnight, noon adds 0.05 to W and raises sea-level air from 7.5 to 9.75 °C; at 1000 m the same samples give 1 and 3.25 °C. Dry water at W = 0 is 1 °C at the surface and 2.5 °C 1000 m down; at W = 1 it is 8 and 6.5 °C. These are conditional examples: W depends on the texture samples at the position, so no fixed temperature follows from the hour alone. The samplers read the regional sampler directly, not the full weather output that adds custom weather and local hazard effects, so those additions do not enter these equations.

Lighting: the update divides the time of day by 3600 × day_length and interpolates a native keyframe table linearly between the first key at or after q and the one before it. The keys sit at 0, 5.76, 7.26, 8.76, 12, 15.48, 16.98, 18.48 and 24 h. The environment file instead places sunrise markers at 6, 7.5 and 9 hours and sunset markers at 16, 17.5 and 19; those names do not occur in the executable and are not the keys. The keys are lighting keyframes, not astronomical or mission sunrise times.

Table: Native lighting keys
| q | Hour | Role (inference from the record order) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.24 | 5.76 | dawn start |
| 0.3025 | 7.26 | dawn middle |
| 0.365 | 8.76 | dawn end |
| 0.5 | 12 | noon |
| 0.645 | 15.48 | dusk start |
| 0.7075 | 16.98 | dusk middle |
| 0.77 | 18.48 | dusk end |

Tornado: each tornado adds a wind vector, capped at length 100, to the weather wind. Outside its core it is I × S × (−100 × a⁸ × (1 − u)² × e + 50 × a² × tangent), with a = 1 − clamp(d ÷ R, 0, 1) for horizontal distance d from the tornado top and outer radius R, u the height fraction from base to top, e the outward horizontal direction and I and S its active factor and strength. The inward pull falls with the eighth power and the swirl with the square, and the pull vanishes at the top; there is no inverse-square law. Inside the core, between base and top, gain = 12 × u³ + 10 ÷ (100 × u + 10) sizes the inner and outer core and the core adds radial, swirl and upward terms with coefficients 200, 200 and 100. The active factor moves by 0.0005 per update, and a damage branch reads the vehicle_damage setting.

Whirlpool: for horizontal distance r from the centre and z = r ÷ 100, the current inside r < 200π is 50 × M × g × (n + tangent), with h = 0.33 ÷ (z² + 0.33) − 0.033, n the normalized vector (−e.x, −h, −e.z) and g = sin(1 ÷ ((z ÷ 2)² + 0.35)) − 0.1. Inside r < 100π the surface drops by 100 × M × h metres and a narrow downward term 500 × M × (0.01 ÷ (z² + 0.01) − 0.001) is added. The whole vector fades linearly from full strength at the depressed surface to 0 at 100 m below it. The environment file's whirlpool forces, 400 vertical, 60 radial and 50 tangential, are not these coefficients. These vectors are wind and current in native units, not forces on a vehicle: what a hull feels depends on the code that consumes them, its shape and its relative motion.

Natural disasters: two shipped addons spawn them. The natural disaster addon lowers a countdown by 1 per onTick call; a slider sets it from 1 to 60 minutes, default 15, and a new save starts at 54000 calls, 15 minutes at 60 calls per second. At 0 it resets and accepts an event with chance D = min(1, (date − 20) ÷ 60), or always with no_clip on, so with no_clip off nothing spawns before date value 20 (inference: the date value counts in-game days). An accepted event is a large wave with weight 0.5, a tornado 0.2, a whirlpool 0.1, a tsunami 0.1, a meteor shower 0.05 or a volcano 0.05, placed 5000 m from player 0 at a random angle; a volcano event erupts the nearest volcano instead. This addon tests no weather, rain or wind.

The mission addon chooses a disaster when it creates a mission, if its Natural Disaster Missions switch is on (the default) and no disaster is pending. With D = min(1, date ÷ 60) it tries, in order and each only if every earlier draw failed: volcano with chance 0.1 + 0.7 × D if a volcano is within 2000 m, meteor 0.1 + 0.3 × D, whirlpool 0.1 + 0.3 × D on a tile with an empty name (open ocean, inference), tsunami 0.1 + 0.3 × D, and tornado 0.1 + 0.9 × D if the wind there exceeds 70. The disaster spawns 60 × 60 × random(30, 60) onTick calls later, 30 to 60 minutes at 60 calls per second. Tornado and meteor spawn 1500 to 2500 m from the mission; the tsunami spawns at the mission position itself once an ocean point 4000 to 8000 m away is found. Neither addon starts forest fires: the fire addon only marks fires the game reports, and native code ignites and spreads them. The two addons are the demonstrated disaster schedulers. spawnVolcano sends network event 115, and its receiver 0x14077dcf0 sets the volcano's is_eruption_triggered flag only when both it and is_erupting are clear; the buildup later clears the first flag and sets the second. Both flags are saved and restored, so a loaded save can resume an eruption without a new scheduling decision. The meteor spawn handler has one direct caller, the network event dispatch, and the other ocean event sends either answer player requests or copy an existing event to a client. A complete exclusion of native scheduling is still open.

Table: Hazard spawning, reach and damage
| Hazard | Natural addon | Mission addon | Direct reach | Damage | Still open |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Large wave | weight 0.5, tsunami of magnitude 0.1 | none | the tsunami band | none in the water sampler | vehicle and character damage |
| Tornado | weight 0.2 | 0.1 + 0.9 × D, wind above 70 | wind 0 from 3000 m off the top (fresh spawn); the vehicle force it enables has no distance test | raycast request of 2500 × S, turned into stored component damage | character damage |
| Whirlpool | weight 0.1, magnitude 1 | 0.1 + 0.3 × D, ocean tile | current 0 from 200π ≈ 628.32 m | none in the water sampler | collision, flooding and drowning damage |
| Tsunami | weight 0.1, magnitude 0.9 | 0.1 + 0.3 × D, magnitude 1 | 0 unless abs(q) < 3.04159283638 | none in the water sampler | collision, flooding and drowning damage |
| Meteor shower | weight 0.05 | 0.1 + 0.3 × D | one main and ten secondaries at M = 1; explosion shell up to about 1548.60 m; the main's tsunami band grows until it fades | explosion of strength size, or 3 × size with the tsunami flag, capped at 10 | block damage falloff, other explosion consumers |
| Volcano | weight 0.05, nearest volcano | 0.1 + 0.7 × D within 2000 m | query radius 10 + (eruption_radius − 10) × f, weighted by the eruption front; heat field without cutoff | component-damage message of 500 to 1000; character damage rate of 3 | lava and projectile contact |
| Lightning EMP | from the weather update | none | 0 from 300 m | electrical interference, not HP | other effects of a strike |
| Forest fire | none | marker only | spread looks 10 m around a wind-offset point each generation | open | lightning and other initial ignition, heat and damage |

Tornado damage: with vehicle_damage on, each pass of the tornado's damage branch picks two points near the lower column and sends one damage raycast request carrying 2500 × S, 2500 for a fresh tornado with S = 1. The server raycasts that segment, drops misses, and queues a record holding the hit vehicle and component, the amount A and s = min(A ÷ 2000, 4), which is 1.25 at S = 1. The scene update drains that queue and sends each record as the component-damage message that volcano hits also use.

Component damage: the component's handler first subtracts a value from the struck component's definition from A and stops unless A stays positive. It then searches voxel cells, 4 per world unit, within clamp(1 − trunc(−4 × s), 0, 16) cells of the hit. Each component found at a rounded distance of d cells gets max(0, trunc((b − d) ÷ 3) + 1) damage units, with b = 4 × trunc(A ÷ 2000) and trunc rounding toward zero, and its stored damage is capped at 50. This is a stepped voxel-distance rule that raises stored component damage; it does not subtract the amount as HP. For a fresh tornado with no deduction, A = 2500 and s = 1.25 give a 6-cell search and b = 4, so a component at d = 0 gets 2 units. The damage lands on what the segment hits, not on everything inside 3000 m. No tornado path to character HP is known.

Tsunami and large wave: both use event type 0 of the water sampler. With r the horizontal distance from the event and A its age in ocean counter steps, q = 0.01 × r − 0.2 × A ÷ 60, and the event adds nothing unless abs(q) < 3.04159283638. That is a ring about 304.16 m either side of r = A ÷ 3, moving outward at 20 m/s if the counter runs 60 steps per second (inference). Inside it the surface rises by H = 100 × M × (1 ÷ (q² + 1) − 0.1) and the current is 12 × (1 + cos φ) × (e.x, clamp(10 × q, −1, 1), e.z), with φ from a 512-entry table that solves φ − 0.8 × sin φ = target. The current fades to 0 at 100 m below the raised surface. At q = 0, H = 90 × M: a 9 m crest for the large wave, 81 m for the natural tsunami and 90 m for the mission tsunami, if M reaches the requested magnitude (inference). No radius is safe at every age: a point the ring has passed gets nothing more from this event, and a point ahead of it is still to be reached.

Meteor shower: the script operator clamps the magnitude M to 0 to 1 and sends one main meteor and trunc(10 × M) secondaries; each recipient gets a copy of the same shower, not extra meteors. With d the randomized incoming direction, the main starts 30000 back along d from the target, with size max(1, 20 × M) and velocity 20 × d. Each secondary aims within ±500 × M of the target horizontally, starts 20000 + U × 15000 × M back, and has size max(1, (0.1 + 0.3 × U) × 20 × M) and velocity (19 + U) × d, each U a separate random draw from 0 to 1. At M = 1, the value both addons pass, that is one size-20 meteor and ten of size 2 to 8. The velocity is a step per scene update: the update raycasts from the position to position + velocity and then adds it, so at a nominal 60 updates per second the main moves at 1200 m/s and the secondaries at 1140 to 1200 m/s (inference). Only the main keeps the caller's tsunami flag, which both addons set; the secondaries pass false.

A meteor that hits land or water reports an impact and is removed. The impact queues an explosion whose strength is the size, or 3 × size with the tsunami flag, and explosion creation caps strength at 10: the main reaches 10 and the secondaries 2 to 8. Strength is an explosion parameter, not HP. The blast radius grows as R = 343 × age, the age advancing 0.0166599992663 per update, and the amplitude falls as 1 − clamp(R ÷ (250 × strength), 0, 1), reaching 0 at 2500 m for strength 10. The shared explosion record lasts 271 updates: creation sets a countdown of 270, and each update runs every consumer before the zero test that removes the record. Its final R is about 1548.60 m, so the amplitude's zero at 2500 m is never reached. Within that shell the body push is min(500000 × strength ÷ R, 30000 × body mass) on bodies between max(0, R − 5.714379787) and R from the centre, and tree processing runs only while R < 20 × strength, under 200 m at the strength cap. Other explosion consumers and meteor block-damage falloff remain open.

The main meteor also starts a tsunami event when it lands less than 3 m above the sampled water height, a texture factor F at the impact exceeds 0.13 and the previous ocean event has faded or has a target below 0.5. F is a byte-texture sample ÷ 255, 1 where the texture is absent, so it is not 1 everywhere. The event is the radial tsunami band above, centred on the impact and started 30 ticks in the past. Its magnitude starts at 0.5, moves toward F by 0.0005555556 per ocean update, holds for 18000 updates and then fades to 0 at the same step. With t the elapsed ticks ÷ 60, the band's outer edge is at (0.2 × t + 3.04159283638) ÷ 0.01 m, so its reach grows with time and ends when the magnitude fades; there is no single time-independent blast radius. For F = 1 the last nonzero update is the 20700th, when the outer edge is about 7214.16 m from the impact if one tick passes per ocean update (inference).

Volcano: each volcano marker in the tile files sets a crater radius and an eruption_radius; the 8 shipped markers use eruption radii from 1000 to 5000 m. Spawning the volcano sets its is_eruption_triggered flag, which starts a buildup; the volcano update later switches to is_erupting. During an eruption the volcano update queries objects within 10 + (eruption_radius − 10) × f, f a per-volcano float. Queried objects pass collision-type, random and phase tests, the phase test being (update counter + body index) & 15 = 0, so a body is tested at most once per 16 updates (inference). Each object gets a spatial weight W = (1 − C((f − 0.7) ÷ 0.3)^5) × (1 − C((y − h) ÷ 50)) × C((y + 10) ÷ 10) × (1 − C((r − front − 2) ÷ 498)), C a clamp to 0 to 1, r the horizontal distance and y the height. The front is 10 + (eruption_radius − 10) × (f − 0.2 × min(4 × f, 1) × B), B an angular byte table ÷ 255, so it is irregular around the crater. h is a height-map sample, a bilinear byte map ÷ 255 times a height field, plus 0.25 × (y0 + 100) − 10, y0 being the volcano centre height. The object-effects handler then forms Q = C((W − 0.9) ÷ 0.1)^10: a positive Q pushes the object and only Q = 1 opens the damage branch, where further random draws pick contact points, hits and amounts. W is a weight, not a per-update chance. With vehicle_damage on, an accepted hit sends the component-damage message with an amount from 500 to 1000 and min(amount ÷ 2000, 4). There b = 0, so without a definition deduction a hit adds at most 1 unit, only to components within 2 cells (inference from the rule above). Characters get a separate message, event 102 with amount 3. It adds −3 to the character's health-change rate for the next character update, which multiplies the rate by dt = elapsed ticks ÷ 60 and a scene integer K and adds the result to the hp value Lua reads. One accepted event therefore removes 3 × dt × K HP, not 3 HP at once, and other health terms and state checks still apply. An active volcano also lowers the air exchange factor of nearby parts such as the Air Scoop Intake 1x1 to max(0.01, 1 − volcanic_heat² × eruption_radius ÷ (2 × distance)), with no distance cutoff, so eruption_radius is not a safe distance. Rendered eruption particles have not yet been connected to physical lava or projectile contact damage.

Forest fire: native code ignites a tree by setting a per-tree intensity byte and adding the tree to its chunk's burning list. Explosions can light an eligible tree with a random intensity of 100 to 199, a position-and-radius ignition lights trees for a queued scene entry of unclassified origin, and burning trees spread. An explosion tests each tree inside its current radius on every update that reaches it: a tree within half the radius first gets a rand() % 10 = 0 destruction draw, and a tree that survives it, or lies in the outer half, gets a rand() % 4 = 0 ignition draw that lights it if it is unlit. These are per-visit chances, not the chance over a whole explosion. The forest manager runs the tree simulation once every 30 manager updates, two per second at 60 manager updates per second (inference). Each tree update reads the rain value R from the full weather output and sets a threshold trunc(100 × R + 100). A burning tree's intensity rises to 255, then falls. While it exceeds the threshold, each tree update tries to spread with a rand() % 25 = 0 test, close to 1 in 25 per tree update. A spread attempt moves the source point by 5 × a, a the manager's wind-derived vector, and lights one unlit tree under 10 m horizontally from that point, at intensity 1; a tree whose search finds none stops trying. Each generation searches around its own wind-offset point, so the 10 m search radius does not bound total spread: after several generations the distance from the first source is only bounded by the sum of 10 + 5 × |a| over them. Rain raises the threshold and so shortens the time each tree can spread (inference). The intensity is a tree state, not a temperature or HP, and 10 m is a search radius, not a fire safe distance.

## How hazard wind and current push a vehicle

Hazard wind and current reach a vehicle by two routes. In the surface route they enter as velocities, not forces. The vehicle update samples the weather wind, tornado wind included, and the hull air callback uses the point velocity v + ω × r minus that wind at each surface point; the water callback subtracts the sampled current the same way. Each callback writes a force and lever arm per surface point. A pass sums the forces and the torques r × F, and the vehicle submits both to its Bullet body, which adds them to the body's total force and torque. The solver turns total force into a velocity change: for a free body with unit linear factors, Δv = F × dt ÷ m, which is F ÷ (60 × m) at dt = 1/60 s. The push therefore depends on the hull's surfaces, shielding, air or water density, drag and lift terms and its own motion. A stationary, unshielded surface sees air moving at minus the sampled wind.

The second route is a direct force that exists only while a tornado does. When the weather list holds at least one flagged tornado entry, the vehicle update adds F = E × (1 − A) × (7.5 × W.x, 30 × W.y, 7.5 × W.z) to vehicles in states 0, 2, 3, 5 and 7. W is the full wind at the vehicle position, ordinary weather wind plus the wind of every tornado; it is not made relative to the vehicle's motion. A is a spatial suppression factor, 1 inside the inner box of a suppression volume and blending to 0 across its outer box; tile loading registers these volumes from tile geometry. E is 0 while the vehicle sits inside another vehicle's compartment and 1 otherwise: each vehicle update recomputes that flag with a compartment query, and the force uses the result from the previous update. The update tests no distance to the tornado, so once a tornado exists, ordinary wind pushes eligible vehicles this way even outside every tornado's wind radius. F goes to the vehicle body with no lever arm, so it adds no torque, and it bypasses the joined-mass cap that part forces such as jet exhaust and propellers pass through. F has no mass factor: the solver multiplies it by inverse mass, so at the same wind a lighter vehicle gains more speed. No vehicle_damage test was found on this route, so it acts with vehicle damage off. This route was traced for vehicles only.

No single force or acceleration applies to every vehicle at a given distance from a tornado; to isolate a tornado's push on one vehicle, compare both routes with and without its wind (inference). The wind cap of 100 bounds each tornado's wind vector, not either force. Each reach above bounds one direct contribution, except the tornado-enabled vehicle force, which has no distance test. None is a safe distance from debris, projectiles, collisions, secondary events or ordinary weather.

findings.label: Natural addon: frequency
findings.value: 1 to 60 min, default 15; a new save starts at 54000
findings.detail: doomsday_frequency is the slider value × 60 × 60 onTick calls. A new save starts the countdown at 15 × 60 × 60 = 54000 calls whatever the slider says; a loaded save keeps its own value.

findings.label: Natural addon: countdown
findings.value: minus 1 per onTick call
findings.detail: onTick ignores its tick_time argument. At 0 the countdown resets to the frequency and the addon tries one event, whether or not one is chosen. Minutes assume 60 calls per second.

findings.label: Natural addon: date gate
findings.value: event only if random < D, D = min(1, (date − 20) ÷ 60)
findings.detail: With no_clip on, D = 1. D ≤ 0 accepts nothing, so with no_clip off no natural disaster spawns before date value 20 (inference: the date value counts in-game days). No weather, rain or wind test appears in this addon.

findings.label: Natural addon: event weights
findings.detail: Probabilities 500/1000, 200/1000, 100/1000, 100/1000, 50/1000 and 50/1000. A second draw walks the table with a running sum; the weights sum to 1, so the pairs order does not change each event's share of accepted attempts.

findings.label: Natural addon: spawn calls
findings.detail: The large wave is a tsunami request with magnitude 0.1.

findings.label: Natural addon: volcano
findings.value: nearest volcano from getVolcanos()
findings.detail: Erupts the volcano nearest the request position, and nothing when the list is empty.

findings.label: Natural addon: spawn position
findings.value: 5000 m from player 0 at a random angle
findings.detail: A spawn distance, not a safe distance.

findings.label: Mission addon: disaster switch
findings.value: Natural Disaster Missions, default on
findings.detail: Independent of the natural addon's frequency slider.

findings.label: Mission addon: selection
findings.detail: Fresh draws in this order, each tried only if every earlier one failed. Nothing is chosen with the switch off or while a disaster is pending. An empty tile name marks open ocean (inference). The chances apply per mission evaluation, not per minute.

findings.label: Mission addon: difficulty
findings.value: D = min(1, date ÷ 60)
findings.detail: With no_clip on, D = 1. Unlike the natural addon there is no 20-day offset.

findings.label: Mission addon: delay
findings.value: 60 × 60 × random(30, 60) onTick calls
findings.detail: Set when the disaster is chosen: 30 to 60 minutes at 60 calls per second.

findings.label: Mission addon: countdown
findings.value: minus 1 per onTick call, spawn at exactly 0
findings.detail: tickDisasters runs once per onTick and does not use delta_worldtime, unlike the mission counter.

findings.label: Mission addon: spawn calls

value.tornado: spawnTornado 1500 to 2500 m from the mission
value.meteor: spawnMeteorShower(offset, 1, true) 1500 to 2500 m from the mission

findings.detail: The tsunami test finds an ocean point but the call passes the mission transform. The offset is 1500 + 1000 × random metres. The volcano is looked up again at spawn time.

findings.detail: The initializer fills φ for target = 2π × j ÷ 512 − π, j = 0 to 511, iterating φ += 0.2 × (target − value) until within 0.00001 (sine calls at 0x1402ba3b3 and 0x1402ba3f3). The sampler interpolates φ linearly between entries. Bytes f3 0f 11 37 at 0x1402ba415, literal e8 68 c8 71 00 at 0x1402ba3b3, literal e8 28 c8 71 00 at 0x1402ba3f3. Report: investigation/hazards.md.

findings.label: Meteor tsunami fade
findings.value: magnitude step 0.0005555556 per ocean update
findings.detail: The ocean update 0x1402bc810 moves the magnitude from 0.5 toward F by this step (0x1402bc86a), counts the hold down, and then subtracts the same step to 0 (0x1402bc93b). For F = 1 that is 900 rise updates, 18000 hold updates, one transition and 1800 fade updates, so the last nonzero update is the 20700th. With one tick per ocean update the band's outer edge is then about 7214.16 m from the impact (inference). Other values of F change the rise length, and a new ocean event can overwrite this one. findings.value: inside half the radius: rand() % 10 = 0 destroys; otherwise rand() % 4 = 0 ignites
findings.detail: For a tree without flag bit 1 inside the current explosion radius, 0x14055a970 first tests the inner half (0.5 × r at 0x14055abfa): there a rand() % 10 = 0 draw (0x14055ad06) takes the destruction branch. A tree that is not destroyed, or lies in the outer half, then gets a rand() % 4 = 0 draw (0x14055ad81) and ignites if it is unlit and has flag bit 0 clear. The explosion repeats these draws on each update that reaches the tree, so they are per-visit chances, not the chance over a whole explosion. Over rand() outputs 0 to 32767 the inner-half ignition share per visit is 29491 ÷ 32768 × 1 ÷ 4, about 22.4998474 percent. Bytes 25 03 00 00 80 at 0x14055ad81, literal f3 44 0f 59 2d b9 50 65 00 at 0x14055abfa, literal 00 00 00 3f at 0x140bafcbc, literal b8 67 66 66 66 at 0x14055ad06. Report: investigation/hazards-rest.md.

findings.label: Meteor spawn handler
findings.value: one direct caller, the event dispatch
findings.detail: The meteor handler 0x14077d710 is called only at 0x14085f718. The meteor pool append also has two callers in save loading, so the handler is not the only producer. Bytes e8 f3 df f1 ff at 0x14085f718. Report: investigation/hazards.md.

findings.label: Volcano activation
findings.value: spawnVolcano → event 115 → 0x14077dcf0
findings.detail: The spawnVolcano operator 0x140725ab0 calls the sender 0x14022cdd0, which writes event 115; table entry 0x140863ba4 leads to the receiver 0x14077dcf0 (call at 0x14085f754). The receiver finds the volcano in the scene collection at +0xbb3a0 (0x14077dd2f) and, only when both +0x60 and +0x61 are clear (0x14077dd36, 0x14077dd3b), sets +0x60 (0x14077dd50) and the update-dirty byte +0x78 (0x14077dd58). That starts the buildup; the volcano update later writes 0x0100 to the pair (0x14055f174), clearing +0x60 and setting +0x61. The earlier attribution of activation to 0x14077d6c0 was wrong: that routine clears a field of another scene collection. Bytes 48 c7 40 08 73 00 00 00 at 0x14022cdf7, literal 45 f7 85 00 at 0x140863ba4, literal e8 97 e5 f1 ff at 0x14085f754, literal 49 03 90 a0 b3 0b 00 at 0x14077dd2f, literal 38 5a 60 at 0x14077dd36, literal 38 5a 61 at 0x14077dd3b, literal c6 42 60 01 at 0x14077dd50, literal c6 42 78 01 at 0x14077dd58, literal 66 c7 47 60 00 01 at 0x14055f174. Report: investigation/hazards-rest.md.

findings.label: Volcano save flags
findings.value: +0x60 is_eruption_triggered, +0x61 is_erupting
findings.detail: The volcano serializer 0x14055e7d0 binds both bytes by these names (0x14055e9a3, 0x14055ea2f) and restores them on load, so a loaded save can resume a buildup or an eruption without a new scheduling decision. Bytes 4c 8d 05 be 9a 62 00 at 0x14055e9a3, literal 69 73 5f 65 72 75 70 74 69 6f 6e 5f 74 72 69 67 67 65 72 65 64 00 at 0x140b88468, literal 4c 8d 05 72 9a 62 00 at 0x14055ea2f, literal 69 73 5f 65 72 75 70 74 69 6e 67 00 at 0x140b884a8. findings.label: Ocean event replication
findings.value: copies stored ocean events to one client
findings.detail: The ocean event send at 0x14084eda2 belongs to connection state replication 0x14084e6e0. It forwards the server's stored ocean event fields to one recipient's queue and draws no new disaster. The other ocean, meteor and volcano sends found sit in request handlers with permission checks. Bytes e8 09 dd 9d ff at 0x14084eda2. Report: investigation/hazards.md.

findings.label: Surface force sum
findings.value: Σ F at +0x928, Σ r × F at +0x934
findings.detail: Each air or water surface callback writes a 0x30-byte record of lever arm and force. The postprocessing pass 0x14048a8f0 sums the forces (0x14048aac3) and the torques r × F (0x14048ab7a); 0x140548570 calls it at 0x14054883d. Bytes f3 0f 11 87 28 09 00 00 at 0x14048aac3, literal f3 0f 11 87 34 09 00 00 at 0x14048ab7a, literal e8 ae 20 f4 ff at 0x14054883d. Report: investigation/hazards.md.

findings.label: Force and torque submission
findings.value: event_set_impulse_threshold and event_set_torque
findings.detail: The summed force goes out through the vtable 0x140b62280 and the torque through 0x140b9a6f8. The force apply slot 0x1401a17b0 calls 0x14019a370 (0x1401a1866) with a zero lever arm, which adds the force to the Bullet total force at body +0x460; the torque slot 0x1401a1960 adds to +0x480. Despite the event name, the force is not an instant velocity change. Bytes f2 0f 58 81 60 04 00 00 at 0x14019a3a3, literal b0 17 1a 40 01 00 00 00 at 0x140b62288, literal 60 19 1a 40 01 00 00 00 at 0x140b9a700, literal e8 05 8b ff ff at 0x1401a1866. Report: investigation/hazards.md.

findings.label: Force to velocity
findings.value: Δv = F × dt ÷ m
findings.detail: Solver setup 0x140128560 multiplies the total force by inverse mass (0x140128734) and by the solver step (0x14012874b) and stores a velocity change (0x140128759). For a free body with unit linear factors that is F ÷ (60 × m) at dt = 1/60 s; torque goes through inverse inertia. The tornado wind cap of 100 limits a velocity, not this force. Bytes f2 41 0f 59 80 60 04 00 00 at 0x140128734, literal f2 41 0f 59 c0 at 0x14012874b, literal 0f 11 82 a0 01 00 00 at 0x140128759. Report: investigation/hazards.md.

findings.label: Tornado force gate
findings.value: a flagged tornado entry anywhere, vehicle state 0, 2, 3, 5 or 7
findings.detail: The vehicle update 0x1404d61f0 skips the branch for an empty weather list (0x1404d6521) and otherwise looks for an entry with byte +0x38 set (0x1404d6551), stopping at the first. The vehicle state at +0x28c must be at most 7 (0x1404d656b) and have its bit set in the mask 0xad (0x1404d64fa, bit test 0x1404d6574), which admits states 0, 2, 3, 5 and 7. The producer has no distance-to-tornado test; each tornado's radius only attenuates its own wind inside the tornado sampler (radius read at 0x1402bea23). The states are known only by number. Bytes 41 0f a3 c6 at 0x1404d6574, literal 0f 84 22 01 00 00 at 0x1404d6521, literal 44 38 64 31 38 at 0x1404d6551, literal 83 f8 07 at 0x1404d656b, literal 41 be ad 00 00 00 at 0x1404d64fa, literal 0f 83 cb 00 00 00 at 0x1404d6578, literal f3 0f 10 4f 4c at 0x1402bea23. Report: investigation/tornado-force.md.

findings.label: Tornado-enabled vehicle force
findings.detail: W is the weather wind at the vehicle position with tornado sampling on (flag at 0x1404d658c, call 0x1402c1830 at 0x1404d659a): ordinary wind plus every tornado's wind, not one tornado's share. The vertical scale is the float 30; the horizontal scale is 30 × 0.25 = 7.5, two multiplies per axis (0x1404d65db, 0x1404d65e0), not a loaded 7.5. A comes from 0x1402c10e0 (call at 0x1404d65ca): 1 inside the inner box of a configured volume, blending across its outer box, the maximum over all volumes; it does not read velocity. 1 − A is formed at 0x1404d65d2. The wind is not made relative to the vehicle's velocity. Bytes f3 44 0f 10 25 fb a1 6d 00 at 0x1404d650c, literal 00 00 f0 41 at 0x140bb0710, literal f3 44 0f 10 05 9e 96 6d 00 at 0x1404d6515, literal 00 00 80 3e at 0x140bafbbc, literal 41 b1 01 at 0x1404d658c, literal e8 91 b2 de ff at 0x1404d659a, literal e8 11 ab de ff at 0x1404d65ca, literal f3 0f 5c d0 at 0x1404d65d2, literal f3 41 0f 59 dc at 0x1404d65db, literal f3 41 0f 59 d8 at 0x1404d65e0, literal f3 41 0f 59 cc at 0x1404d65ee, literal f3 41 0f 59 c4 at 0x1404d6604, literal f3 41 0f 59 c0 at 0x1404d6609. Report: investigation/tornado-force.md.

findings.label: Tornado force vehicle flag
findings.value: E = 0 when vehicle byte +0x61c is set, else 1
findings.detail: The test at 0x1404d659f selects 1 when the byte is zero (0x1404d65a6) and otherwise a zeroed register (0x1404d65a8). Bytes 44 38 a7 1c 06 00 00 at 0x1404d659f, literal 74 06 at 0x1404d65a6, literal 41 0f 28 f2 at 0x1404d65a8. Report: investigation/tornado-force.md.

findings.label: Uncapped tornado force submission
findings.value: force event 0x1401a7470, not the joined-mass cap 0x1401a7ad0
findings.detail: The call at 0x1404d6644 goes to the plain force-event helper, which skips a zero vector and copies F unchanged with a zero lever arm (0x1404d6625), so it adds no torque. It never reaches the cap helper's length comparison (0x1401a7b66), which limits part forces to k times the summed adjusted mass of the joined bodies (the k × S cap of investigation/force-cap.md; that S is not tornado strength). The event consumer 0x1401a16a0 (table slot 0x140b82d38) adds F to the body force at +0x460 (0x14019a3c2). No vehicle_damage test was found from the update entry through this chain. Bytes e8 27 0e cd ff at 0x1404d6644, literal 4c 89 65 f0 at 0x1404d6625, literal c6 44 24 20 01 at 0x1404d662d, literal a0 16 1a 40 01 00 00 00 at 0x140b82d38, literal 0f 2f d0 at 0x1401a7b66, literal 76 28 at 0x1401a7b69, literal f2 0f 11 81 60 04 00 00 at 0x14019a3c2. Report: investigation/tornado-force.md.

findings.label: Tornado force and mass
findings.value: no mass factor in F; the solver applies inverse mass
findings.detail: Solver setup 0x140128560 reads the body's inverse mass (0x14012865a) and multiplies it into the accumulated force (0x140128734) with its integration factor. F itself does not scale with mass, so at the same wind a lighter body gains more speed from it. A body with zero inverse mass gets no linear change. Bytes f2 41 0f 10 90 d0 03 00 00 at 0x14012865a, literal f2 41 0f 59 80 60 04 00 00 at 0x140128734. Report: investigation/tornado-force.md.

findings.label: Vehicle compartment flag
findings.value: byte +0x61c set while the vehicle is inside another vehicle's compartment
findings.detail: Later in the same update 0x1404d61f0 clears the byte (0x1404d771b) and tests candidate vehicles with 0x14048e810 (0x1404d77c0), which maps the point into the candidate's voxel grid and looks up its compartment. A hit sets the byte (0x1404d77cd) and stores the candidate and compartment index at +0x620 to +0x628. The force reads the byte before this recomputation, so it uses the previous update's result. The description is inferred from the compartment lookup; no field name was recovered. Bytes c6 87 1c 06 00 00 01 at 0x1404d77cd, literal c6 87 1c 06 00 00 00 at 0x1404d771b, literal e8 4b 70 fb ff at 0x1404d77c0. Report: investigation/hazards-rest.md.

findings.label: Weather suppression boxes
findings.value: registered from tile-loaded geometry
findings.detail: Tile loading 0x14056e2c0 walks its +0x1a8 entries, keeps those with +0x200 = 0, and registers each transform and inner and outer bounds with the weather manager (call at 0x14056e566). 0x1402c10e0 evaluates the stored boxes and takes the largest suppression. Which tile XML element authors these boxes is open. Bytes e8 85 29 d5 ff at 0x14056e566. Report: investigation/hazards-rest.md.

limitations: Native findings are static readings of this executable build. No game process was executed, and no value here was checked in play.

The texture values at named map sites were not recovered, so no site-specific temperature is given. The seasonal term uses the serialized numeric month, but its mapping to displayed calendar labels was not traced, so the warmest named in-game month is not established.

Tornado character damage was not traced, and neither was any tsunami or whirlpool damage beyond their physical water effects. The meaning of the component-definition value subtracted before component damage, and the scene multiplier K in character HP integration, were not established.

Meteor block-damage falloff and the bounds of explosion consumers outside the shared record, such as the separate record the impact queues through 0x14077e720, were not traced. The main meteor's texture factor F was not mapped across the world.

Rendered eruption particles were not connected to physical lava or projectile contact damage, and the object-kind, update-phase and raycast tests that still qualify the eruption damage branch were not decoded.
Lightning ignition, the origin of the scene's queued position ignitions, any other initial-fire scheduling and vehicle and character heat damage from fires were not traced.
An exhaustive exclusion of native disaster scheduling was not established: indirect calls, script operator invocations, load and clone paths and every writer of the volcano flags were not ruled out.

The wind and current force chain was not traced in full: the cached current grid, surface geometry weights, shielding eligibility, wind and current consumers besides the surface route and the tornado-enabled vehicle force, and the kilograms per editor mass unit.

The tornado-enabled force was traced for vehicles only. A matching character, carried-object or debris path was not established, and neither were the names of vehicle states 0, 2, 3, 5 and 7, the serialized name of the compartment flag, the tile XML element that authors the suppression volumes, the integration factor and substeps the solver applies to it, or the scheduling above the vehicle update.

articles.title: Jet startup, turbines and afterburners
articles.summary: Jet component descriptions separate electrical startup, combustion and exhaust controls.
articles.body: The compressor requires electrical power to begin compression. The combustion chamber takes jet fuel and throttle from 0 to 1, and its tooltip says combustion begins when internal pressure is high enough without giving a threshold. Turbines convert air pressure to RPS. The medium turbine documents a torque connection for motor startup or driving props and generators. The afterburner adds thrust at increased fuel consumption. Its thrust spoiler input runs from 0 for no reduction to 1 for total reduction. The separate Turbine Engine part (turbine.xml) is not a jet part: a native decode (investigation/classic-engines.md) found it runs the classic diesel engine update, so its engine_max_force of 100000 says nothing about jet turbines. A native decode of the modular jet update (investigation/jet-engines.md, shown on the Jet engines parts pages) found that combustion needs internal RPS strictly above 0.5, not a pressure threshold. The effective throttle u is clamped to 0 to 1 and limited by the jet fuel in the chamber, which burns 0.12 × u × RPS L/s. The compressor, enabled and powered, requests 0.1 charge per update, transfers 0.2 × (100 × r0 - (p_out - p_in)) of pressure state and loses 0.0001 times that transfer in RPS after its starter input and 0.99 retention. Combustion adds 1600 × u × RPS pressure and 0.1 × u × RPS internal temperature per update. Turbines halve the incoming pressure, gain 0.0000375 × pressure RPS when undamaged and charge their Electric connection. The power connection of the medium turbine submits its RPS with shaft weight 160. Exhaust force is 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000), scaled by altitude, the thrust spoiler and an afterburner multiplier of 1 + 500 × the jet fuel stored in the exhaust, and capped at 100 × S, S being the summed adjusted mass of the bodies joined by joints (investigation/force-cap.md). RPS reaches the exhaust only through the pressure the chamber adds. A later decode (investigation/leftovers.md) found no jet-fuel debit in the afterburner: its Fuel port exchange fills the buffer or returns fuel, and its purge of other liquids skips jet fuel, so with the buffer level steady the afterburner draws 0 L/s. The tooltip's increased fuel consumption has no counterpart in that code; more stored fuel raises thrust, not burn. A later decode (investigation/misc-gaps.md) found how the parts connect: a port at grid cell p facing n joins only a part with a port at exactly p + n facing back, and the search passes through ducts and every splitter branch, skipping ducts it has already visited, to the next active jet parts. An intake that the shared grid lookup pairs with no other part sets its outgoing pressure to 0.1 × its signed forward speed × clamp(1 - 1.5 × height ÷ 40000, 0, 1), and the large intake also pushes along its axis with 2600 × (RPS - 5) × that altitude factor above 5 RPS.

These are supplied resources. No game process was executed, and native code loading, overrides and effective runtime values remain unverified.

The ignition, fuel, compressor, combustion, turbine and exhaust equations come from that native decode. Physical units of jet pressure and temperature were not established, and SI torque, power and efficiency were not recovered. The equilibrium and startup time of an assembled engine were not traced: the duct and splitter search is decoded, but how merged and attached assemblies supply the body map it searches was not. The intake's pairing partner and the sources behind its source sample were not traced either. The medium turbine port described as torque carries RPS with solver weight 160, not a torque in N m.

articles.title: Fireboxes, boilers and condensers
articles.summary: A firebox burns at most 0.00002 × voxels coal per update and heats its coolant; boilers and condensers convert water and steam at a fixed temperature of 100, at min(0.001 × (T - 100), water) per update when boiling.
articles.body: The coal firebox consumes one coal to ignite and provides air, exhaust and coolant connections. The boiler tooltip recommends a firebox heat supply and controlling evaporation to maintain consistent output steam pressure. Its labelled Water In and Steam Out ports have no descriptions. The condenser converts steam back to water and should be continuously cooled; its coolant descriptions explicitly call for cold fluid. A native decode (investigation/steam.md, shown on the Steam parts pages) found that the firebox requests 0.00002 × voxels × clamp((600 - T) ÷ 400, 0, 1) coal per update, at most 0.054 and 0.21 per simulated second for the small and large firebox. It burns only while Air pressure is more than 1 above Exhaust pressure and oxygen covers the request at a 0.21 reference fraction, and each unit of coal burned adds 200 to the fire temperature. The fire loses 0.001 of its gap to the surroundings per update and exchanges heat with its coolant at k = 0.0008 × voxels, the fire weighted 400. Boilers and condensers convert in their phase chamber at a fixed temperature of 100, whatever the pressure: at or above 100, min(0.001 × (T - 100), water) per update becomes steam, 1:1 by stored amount; below 100, min(0.001 × (100 - T), 0.1 × steam) condenses. Phase and coolant chambers exchange heat at k = 0.1 × (1 - D), D = clamp(0.1 × damage, 0, 1), weighted by liquid amount, and lose 0.0001 of their gap to the surroundings per update. Boiler Water In admits fresh water one way in with bias -60, and Steam Out passes steam one way out with bias 2.5 × steam ÷ phase volume; the condenser's Steam In and Water Out are the reverse with no bias, and the coolant ports enforce no direction. The port solver's 0 to 60 target clamp is a flow rule, not a pressure limit, and the boiler, condenser and phase code contain no pressure limit or burst test. A later decode (investigation/drivetrain-gaps.md) found that ignition writes 3600 to a state the combustion code only tests for nonzero, with no countdown in those paths, and that a hot damaged firebox can queue a component and body event through a shared helper when the vehicle_damage setting is on.

articles.title: Steam turbines and piston timing
articles.summary: The turbine turns steam flow into a target RPS that keeps 0.985 per update; the piston switches its own ports at half turn and drives its crank by 0.002 × steam pressure difference × sin(2πz).
articles.body: The turbine tooltip says torque comes from the force generated by steam passing through it. Its Steam In, Steam Out and RPS ports are labels without descriptions. The piston tooltip says outer-coupling pressure extends the piston and inner-coupling pressure retracts it. Alternating pressure according to piston position allows the crankpin to rotate continuously. The piston also has labelled Piston Position and RPS signals and two described power connections. A native decode (investigation/steam.md, shown on the Steam parts pages) found that the turbine passes gas one way from Steam In to Steam Out through the pump solver with flow factor 0.0025, so exhaust pressure at or above inlet pressure stops it, and it consumes no steam. Each update its speed gains 1000 × the steam moved, is multiplied by 0.985 and is submitted as target RPS with shaft weight 65 on each RPS port; unloaded it settles at 0.985 ÷ 0.015 × 1000 × the steam moved per update. The piston's crank phase z runs 0 to 1 turns and is the Piston Position output. Each chamber has a Steam In and a Steam Out, and the update opens one of each pair by half turn, switching at z = 0.5, so no external valve timing is needed. Each update it adds 0.002 × (p_B - p_A) × sin(2πz) to its crank group, p being chamber pressure times steam fraction, and submits the group speed with shaft weight 20 × voxels per port. The render crank radii 0.075, 0.146 and 0.216 suggest strokes of 0.15, 0.292 and 0.432 world units (inference). A later decode (investigation/drivetrain-gaps.md) found the crank group integration: at the end of each update speed = clamp(0.99 × (speed + drive), −10, 10), the drive is cleared and the phase advances by speed ÷ 60 turns with floor wrapping, so the speed is in RPS and capped at 10. Before that, each connected RPS port replaces the group speed with its shaft group's published speed, which is how a shaft load slows the crank.

articles.title: Nuclear fuel assemblies and control rods
articles.summary: Fuel assemblies add the reactions of up to four coupled fuel assemblies, control rods scale the excess over 0.1 × fuel by 1 − 0.01 × insertion, and fuel rods heat by 0.1 × r per update and take damage above 1500.
articles.body: A fuel rod can be inserted into a fuel assembly to begin fission. The assembly tooltip says fuel rods consume uranium ingots from workbench inventory to fuel. A control rod decreases the reaction rate of adjacent rods. The assembly labels Release Fuel Rod and Fuel Rod Temperature, while the control rod labels Insertion Target and Insertion; their port descriptions are empty. A native decode (investigation/nuclear.md, shown on the Nuclear parts pages) names the three nuclear_component_type values from the editor selector: 0 fuel assembly, 1 fuel rod and 2 control rod. Each update an assembly with a rod computes A = b + 0.999 × (R − b), B = S + 0.998 × (A − S) and b + (1 − 0.01 × C) × (B − b), with b = 0.1 × fuel fraction, R the rod's reaction, S the summed reaction of coupled fuel assemblies and C the summed insertion of coupled control rods; the rod then clamps its reaction r to 0 to 50. Adjacency is the four control_rod couplings x+, x-, z+ and z-, not a radius, so an assembly sees at most four neighbours, fuel or control. A later decode (investigation/misc-gaps.md) found that two couplings link only when each sits at the other's grid cell plus its outward direction, one cell apart and facing each other, with alignment vectors equal or exactly opposite; there is no distance or angle tolerance. Insertion follows Insertion Target clamped to 0 to 1 by at most 0.005 per update, 200 updates or 3.333 s for a full stroke; larger insertion lowers the reaction but never below the 0.1 × fuel baseline. A rod uses 1e-8 × r of its fuel per update, so a full rod lasts 33333 s, 9.259 simulated hours, at r = 50. It heats by 0.1 × r per update, exchanges heat with immersed coolant at k = 0.001 × (q ÷ A) × w, the rod counting as 100 liquid amount and its own step capped at 0.5, and moves 0.001 of the way to its surroundings. A rod above r = 0.001 is a live radiation source of strength s = 0.1 × r with linear falloff over 10 × s metres, cut by 200 m across compartments, and assemblies add 0.001 × reaction ÷ A to their coolant's contamination, which a radiation detector inside reads. Strictly above 1500 a rod takes damage at once and then every 300 hot updates, up to 50; the update has no separate meltdown or explosion temperature.

articles.title: Gear ratios and clutch engagement
articles.summary: Gearboxes pull RPS B toward the selected ratio × RPS A, so for N:1 the A side is fast; the standalone clutch couples with strength input^6 and the modular clutch follows input^3 with a slew.
articles.body: The selected gearbox definitions expose power connections A and B, an electrical connection and a Gear Switch input. Their tooltips say the switch toggles between two property values. The torque_gearbox_2 tooltip states an operating torque difference up to 4000 without specifying a unit. The standard clutch takes engagement from 0 to 1 and says this controls transmitted power. The modular clutch attaches to a crankshaft to control torque made available to the connected system. A native decode (investigation/transmission.md, shown on the Transmission parts pages) found that every gearbox offers the same eight ratios: 1:-1, 1:1, 6:5, 3:2, 9:5, 2:1, 5:2 and 3:1, as multipliers q = -1, 1, 5/6, 2/3, 5/9, 1/2, 2/5 and 1/3. The gearbox stores q on RPS A and 1 ÷ q on RPS B, and the shaft solver pulls RPS B toward q × RPS A, so for an N:1 option RPS A is the fast side and RPS B targets A ÷ N. The two sides stay separate shaft groups. Each update a group adds the other side's speed with path weight h = 0.95 × c, where c is 1 for an intact gearbox, adding sign(q) × v × I × h to its numerator and I × h ÷ |q| to its weight; paths with h at or below 0.001 add nothing. This is a weighted speed exchange with no slip threshold, and 0.95 is not a 95% power efficiency: two groups already at the ratio stay there. Gear Switch picks Ratio Off or Ratio On, and a new ratio replaces the old one in the same update while the gearbox has any electrical availability; without power it keeps the last ratio and stays coupled. The standalone clutch sets c = e × clamp(input, 0, 1)^6 directly each update, with e = min(1, availability ÷ 0.01), so input 0.5 gives 1/64 and an isolated clutch transfers nothing below about 0.319. The modular clutch is separate code: its engagement moves toward clamp(input, 0, 1)^3 by at most 0.1 per update. Nonzero damage sets a gearbox's or standalone clutch's coupling to 0. The gearbox force_emitter_max_force values (200, 1200 and 5000; 1000 and 9999999 for the legacy definitions) are copied at binding but not used as a solver weight, so they are not torque capacities. A later decode (investigation/drivetrain-gaps.md) found that gearbox and clutch damage goes through a shared setter capped at 50 and that a shared repair routine lowers damage by an amount its caller passes, never below 0. A shaft rebuild clears every registered connection's group pointer before the old groups are freed, then forms new groups in connection-discovery order and drops groups with fewer than two members.

findings.detail: Slot +0x20 of the torque component vtable (0x140b66730) selects this shared setter, which keeps the smaller unsigned value and stores it as damage. Bytes b8 32 00 00 00 3b d0 0f 42 c2 89 41 08 at 0x140325ab0, literal b0 5a 32 40 01 00 00 00 at 0x140b66730. Report: investigation/drivetrain-gaps.md.

articles.title: Underwater propellers and pitch control
articles.summary: Marine propellers push only with the hub at or below the water surface, and pitch is a normalized -1 to 1 value in a decoded RPS and flow law.
articles.body: The small boat propeller receives engine power and its tooltip says it operates only underwater. The controllable-pitch boat propeller also requires underwater operation and takes desired pitch from -1 to 1. Its force_emitter_max_force field is 80000 versus 20000 for the selected small fixed-pitch propeller. A native decode (investigation/propulsion.md, shown on the Propulsion parts pages) found that every propeller, rotor and ducted fan runs one force-emitter update. Each update it scales the published shaft speed by 0.9999 to w, forms the effective pitch p = clamp(saved pitch + Pitch input, -1, 1) and the load b = (2 × w × rotation_speed × π × blade_physics_length × p × 0.75 + p × U) × blade_efficiency × intact blades × 0.32, where U is minus the hub's velocity through still water along the thrust axis, signed by the pitch. With K = force_emitter_max_force ÷ 1000, or F × intact blades ÷ 8000 for the pitchable propellers, q = clamp(b ÷ 2K, -10, 10) is multiplied by 10 below the water surface; the propeller removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its shaft and pushes with 1500 × K × removed RPS, signed by the pitch, in the game's internal force unit. Thrust is queued only when the hub is at or below the sampled water surface; the shaft load applies either way. force_emitter_max_force is therefore a solver weight, not a thrust ceiling: at 10 RPS and pitch 1 the small fixed propeller gives about 22201 internal force, and the small, standard and large pitchable propellers about 4074, 20411 and 35002 per RPS. Pitch is a normalized number, not a blade angle; zero pitch gives no load and no thrust. A separate application cap of 100 × S limits the force actually applied.

articles.title: Aircraft propellers and rotor controls
articles.summary: Rotor and propeller inputs are normalized pitch and cyclic values in a decoded thrust, shaft-load and force-geometry law.
articles.body: The aircraft propeller takes collective from -1 to 1, and its tooltip links thrust to received engine torque without giving an equation. The selected large helicopter rotor has roll, pitch and collective inputs from -1 to 1. Its tooltip describes pitch and roll control through the swashplate and says force decreases underwater. The tail rotor takes yaw from -1 to 1 to control generated force. A native decode (investigation/propulsion.md, shown on the Propulsion parts pages) found one force-emitter update for all of them. The effective pitch is clamp(saved pitch + Collective, -1, 1), a normalized number, not degrees or turns; the saved pitch starts at force_emitter_default_pitch, 1 for the main rotors and the aircraft propeller and 0 for the tail rotor, so Collective -1 gives zero thrust on a main rotor and the tail rotor's Yaw is a signed pitch. From the shaft speed, pitch and air-relative flow the part computes a load b, removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its shaft with q = clamp(b ÷ 2K, -10, 10), and pushes with 1500 × K × removed RPS × efficiency, where K = force_emitter_max_force ÷ 1000 or ÷ 2000 with 4 intact blades. Roll and Pitch move the force point by -4 × input along local X and Z and tilt its direction by 0.4 × input. Thrust is scaled by (1 - 2.2413793e-5 × altitude)^5.3595023, 0 above 40000. With the hub below the water surface the scalar update gives no thrust and multiplies q by 10, so the rotor brakes its shaft; that is the decreased underwater force. A physical rotor hinge gets a motor with impulse limit 1000, and coaxial rotors add an opposing force pair of 800 × b × clamp(|pitch + Collective + 0.1|, 0, 1) about the rotor axis.
