articles.title: Weapon loading, ammunition and timed fuses
articles.summary: Guns fire at a fixed muzzle speed per weapon class, barrel length sets only the muzzle position, and loading runs on per-class breech and receiver timers; Fuse Timer detonates fragmentation rounds, and high-explosive rounds from the heavy autocannon up, at an interpolated point.
articles.body: The light autocannon trigger feeds, loads and fires cartridges from connected belts or drums. Its tooltip requires electricity for loading. The selected small drum has weapon_ammo_capacity 100, reports ammo count and cannot mix calibers. Feeder belts use electrical power to transfer cartridges in the arrow direction. The battle cannon trigger fires a loaded shell, and Open Breech permits loading. Its optional Fuse Timer is explicitly in seconds for high-explosive and fragmentation ammunition. A native decode (investigation/weapons.md, shown on the Weapons parts pages) found that weapon_class selects one of seven gun records. Muzzle speed is 800, 1000, 1000, 900, 800, 700 and 600 m/s for the machine gun, light, rotary and heavy autocannon, battle, artillery and Bertha cannon, added to the firing body's velocity; weapon_barrel_length_voxels only places the muzzle, at 0.175 + 0.25 per voxel of the gun and each barrel extension or muzzle brake. Each update a round moves by velocity ÷ 60, loses 0.5 × (138750 ÷ (138750 + height))² m/s of vertical speed, 30 m/s² at sea level, and keeps 0.975, 0.98, 0.99, 0.995, 0.998, 0.999 or 0.9995 of its velocity; in water the step is 0.2 and the retention × 0.8. Rounds are removed after 300 updates from the machine gun and the light and rotary autocannon, 600 from the heavy autocannon and 3600 from the cannons, and machine-gun and autocannon rounds are also removed below 50 m/s. Spread is two independent angles within ±0.25 × dispersion × m radians, dispersion 0.01, 0.02 for the rotary autocannon and 0.005 for artillery and Bertha, and each barrel extension lowers m by 0.2 to at least 0.5 without changing muzzle speed. Impact magnitude is B × speed ÷ 1000 for kinetic rounds, × 0.4 for armour-piercing and × 0.65 for incendiary, and B or 0.4 × B for high explosive or fragmentation, with B from 0.1 to 4; explosions search within 7.5 × that magnitude in metres. Armour-piercing rounds lose 100 × p × mass ÷ cells of speed per struck cell. Breech transitions take 2, 4, 1, 16, 75, 250 and 600 updates and the battle, artillery and Bertha receivers wait 30, 90 and 240 updates after a round arrives, the heavy autocannon 6. Inferred from that state machine, the automatic guns cycle at most at 900, 450, 1800 and about 94.7 rounds per minute. Drums hold their weapon_ammo_capacity of light rounds, half in rotary rounds and a fifth in heavy rounds. Fuse Timer applies to fragmentation rounds, and to high-explosive rounds on the heavy autocannon and the cannons: T = max(1/60, input + 0.02 × u - 0.01) s with u random from 0 to 1, and the round detonates in the update where (age + 1) ÷ 60 reaches T, interpolated within that update.

articles.title: Composite data over electrical cables
articles.summary: A composite value is 32 on/off channels and 32 binary32 numbers, numbered 1 to 32, in 132 bytes. Wires, microprocessor bridges and Electrical Cable Anchors copy it whole, and anchors also pass a video descriptor and a private copy of the audio samples.
articles.body:
The electrical cable anchor tooltip permits one rope logic link between two anchors, carrying data and electricity. Its ports are composite, on/off, video and audio send and receive pairs. A native check (investigation/config.md) of the scalar input getter 0x1408cacf0 found that it copies a cached value and returns, so reading an input does not evaluate the upstream graph.

A native decode (investigation/composite.md, shown on the Electrical Cable Anchor, Microprocessor and Logic pages) recovered the value and every copy of it. The value starts with a 32-bit on/off mask, channel c at bit c - 1, followed by 32 numbers, channel c at byte 4 × c, so channel 32 starts at byte 128. Lua getBool and getNumber return false and 0 outside 1 to 32. This is the in-memory value, not a network or save format.

Table: Composite value
| Part | Where | Channel c |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On/off mask | 32-bit word at byte 0 | bit c - 1 |
| Numbers | 32 binary32 values from byte 4 | byte 4 × c |

Wires: the dispatcher first runs every component update, then goes through the vehicles one at a time. For each vehicle it runs the transport pass, which holds the cable copy, and then flushes that vehicle's outputs: each output pushes its value into the cache of every input wired to it. Inference: on an ordinary wire a consumer reads a new value one update after the producer wrote it.

Cables: an anchor reads its linked peer and, while both states are below 5, copies its Composite Input value, all 132 bytes, to the peer's Composite Output, its on/off input to the peer's On/Off Output, its video descriptor to the peer's Video Data Receive and its audio samples to the peer's Audio Data Receive. Video is copied by value with no allocation; audio goes into a buffer the receiving anchor owns. Electric Cable Pulleys (subtype 9) route the same copies through their own buffers. A later decode (investigation/misc-gaps.md) found how the links are set up: each end stores its peer per side, a connection named Rope 2 in the second link slot (+0xaa0) and any other in the first (+0xa98), so the two ends of one link can use different slots. A pulley hands what one side receives straight to the peer on its other side in the same pass. A value crosses several pulleys in one pass when they are processed in route order, and each hop whose next pulley is processed earlier adds a pass: passes = 1 + the number of such reversals. Because cable copies and output flushes interleave vehicle by vehicle, a write to an anchor on another vehicle can land before or after that vehicle's flush, so the number of updates a cable adds depends on vehicle order.

Microcontrollers: composite bridges copy the whole value, video bridges the descriptor and audio bridges the samples. The editor limits width and length to 1 to 6, and upload rejects anything above 6.

articles.title: Winch controls, length and hose connections
articles.summary: Winch descriptions document electrical operation, length telemetry and hose-coil ports. Rope-node winches reel at 0.012 × cable_length × Speed m/s; legacy winches and the Hose reel at 0.24 × Speed m/s at full electricity.
articles.body: The selected mechanical winch raises its cable on Up and lowers it on Down. Length reports the current cable length in metres. The selected large variant documents the same controls and units. Their short tooltips describe 20m and 100m mechanical winches respectively. Both expose electrical and hose-coil fluid connections. A native decode (investigation/winches.md, shown on the winch, Hose and winch end parts pages) found two reel implementations. Rope-node winches (type 48, Small, Medium, Large and Huge at 10, 40, 150 and 600 m) step the rope by 0.0002 × cable_length × Speed metres per update: 0.12, 0.48, 1.8 and 7.2 m/s at the default Speed 1, editor range 0.1 to 10. Both ends of a rope share one limit, the sum of their cable_length values, and a step is kept only while the length stays above 0.1 m and below that sum, so a step that would cross a bound is dropped rather than clamped. A Speed input from -1 to 1 replaces the buttons at a magnitude of 0.1 or more. Holding both buttons cancels. After each accepted step the winch requests 0.01 charge units (0.6 per second); the reply does not scale the step, and with no usable electricity the buttons are ignored. Static inference: the Speed input bypasses that gate. Legacy winches (type 20: Small, Medium, Large and Huge at 10, 20, 100 and 500 m) and the 16 m Hose step by 0.004 × Speed × p metres per update, p being the supplied fraction of a 0.01 charge request made for each held control: 0.24 m/s at Speed 1 and full supply for every size, editor range 0.1 to 5. Their rest length is clamped to 0.25 m to cable_length, both inclusive. Holding both controls cancels at full supply and costs two requests; under shortage Up is served first, so the rope shortens. The winch end pieces are the far attachment and fluid end of their winch, with no reel of their own; all five end-piece files are identical, and the Large and Huge Winches both use winch_b. Hose coils and rope hoses link the two fluid networks without a length term, so a longer cable adds no hose volume or flow loss (Hose and winch part articles).

The reel rates, length limits, charge requests, simultaneous controls and hose exchange come from that native decode. Rates are changes of the rope's rest length; travel of a loaded hook was not measured. Still not recovered: a force-equivalent rope stiffness. The rope is a Bullet soft-body chain whose material coefficients are 1 without a conversion to N/m. The decoded reel and rope paths have no maximum tension, maximum solver impulse or tensile snapping threshold: rope-node ropes get an uncapped corrective impulse min(K_A, K_B) × (D - L) when stretched beyond their length, neither reel routine compares a force with a break threshold, and the explicit rope removal is called from requests, endpoint cleanup and endpoint control state, not from a force or strain test. Whether the Bullet link solver or collision and damage code caps the load or severs a rope was not traced.

articles.title: Magnetic connectors, transfers and hardpoints
articles.summary: Connector tooltips specify attachment conditions and distinguish release from launch. Small, fluid, electric, torque and hardpoint connectors attach under 0.5 m between centres, hinge and large connectors under 0.25 m with their samples lined up; magnet_force scales only the pull before attaching.
articles.body: Small magnetic connectors require proximity and both magnets switched on. Electric and fluid connector tooltips describe attachment by proximity and free transfer of their respective resources when connected. Torque connectors document mechanical-energy transfer. These connectors report attachment and expose composite and video send/receive ports. Hardpoint bodies require correct alignment and transfer logic and fluid. Release disconnects; Launch also activates the attached ordnance, with a Launched output on the attachment. A native decode (investigation/connectors.md, shown on the connector, hardpoint and Mag All part pages) gives the rules. A connector searches 10 m for a partner of the same connector_type, or the other half of a hardpoint pair. Small, fluid, electric and torque connectors and hardpoints attach when the centres are under 0.5 m apart, hinge and large connectors under 0.25 m. Large, hinge and hardpoint connectors also need each of their samples (four rim points, two axis endpoints or two axial points, 0.25 m from the centre) within 0.1118 m of a partner sample. Before attaching, small, hinge and large connectors pull each update with F = 60 × magnet_force × P × W × d ÷ (1 + |d|²) for offsets under 1 m, P being the electrical supply factor and W the lighter body's native weight field; rim and endpoint samples pull at gain 0.15. Fluid, electric, torque and hardpoint connectors carry definition flag 0x100000, which removes the pull and makes their Release input start a 120-update (2 s) detach that holding the input keeps restarting. Attached pairs are held by a Bullet joint: point-to-point for small, fluid, electric and torque connectors, hinge for hinge connectors, fixed for large connectors and hardpoints. Its break threshold is the largest double and the attach routine never reads magnet_force, so magnet_force (0.1, 0.15, 0.2) is not a holding force. While linked, each update copies the composite signal (32 on/off channels and 32 numbers), on/off and number signals and the video source straight to the partner, with no buffer or averaging. Fluid moves between the two networks through the two-port solver at factor 0.5 and bias 0; electric connectors and hardpoints join their electrical networks into one charge pool; large and torque connectors link their shaft nodes. A hardpoint attachment sends its ordnance type code to the body's Ordinance Type output: 1 Utility, 2 Fuel, 3 Unguided bomb, 4 Laser Guided Bomb, 5 GPS Guided Bomb, 6 Rocket, 7 Rocket Pod, 8 Laser Guided Missile, 9 GPS Guided Missile, 10 Radar Guided Missile, 11 Torpedo, 12 Cannon. Launch sets a latch on the attachment, output as Launched, and detaches it like Release. The Mag All grabs whatever touches a 0.125 m contact sphere with a point-to-point joint. Its Force output is the joint's absolute solver impulse in internal units, and it lets go above 200 × the electrical supply factor, then waits 30 updates.

The attachment distances, pull, joint types, release timing, signal copies, fluid factor, electrical pool bridge, ordnance codes and Launch latch come from that native decode.
